text: June fourteenth... <#0.45#> twenty fifteen.
display: June 14th, 2015.

text: In the quiet town of Springfield, Missouri.
display: In the quiet town of Springfield, Missouri.

text: On the shared Facebook page of the best-known mother and daughter in the area — <#0.15#> Dee Dee Blanchard and her daughter Gypsy Rose, who everyone believed was severely disabled — <#0.15#> a short, bitter status suddenly appeared, announcing that Dee Dee was dead... <#0.45#> and the whole neighborhood fell silent.
display: On the shared Facebook page of the best-known mother and daughter in the area — Dee Dee Blanchard and her daughter Gypsy Rose, who everyone believed was severely disabled — a short, bitter status suddenly appeared, announcing that Dee Dee was dead, and the whole neighborhood fell silent.

text: Neighbors immediately gathered around the small pastel-pink house where the two of them lived.
display: Neighbors immediately gathered around the small pastel-pink house where the two of them lived.

text: To understand why a single status update caused such a shock, let us hear from a resident of the same street — <#0.15#> one of the people who watched the life of this mother and daughter for many years.
display: To understand why a single status update caused such a shock, let us hear from a resident of the same street — one of the people who watched the life of this mother and daughter for many years.

text: To all of us, that pink house was a symbol of sacred motherly love.
display: To all of us, that pink house was a symbol of sacred motherly love.

text: Dee Dee was a remarkable single mother who devoted her whole life to caring for her daughter Gypsy Rose — <#0.15#> an unfortunate girl with a long list of grave illnesses: paralysis from the waist down, leukemia, muscular dystrophy, severe epilepsy, and the mind of a seven-year-old.
display: Dee Dee was a remarkable single mother who devoted her whole life to caring for her daughter Gypsy Rose — an unfortunate girl with a long list of grave illnesses: paralysis from the waist down, leukemia, muscular dystrophy, severe epilepsy, and the mind of a seven-year-old.

text: Everyone in this town was moved to tears by how much she sacrificed for her child.
display: Everyone in this town was moved to tears by how much she sacrificed for her child.

text: But when police entered that cold, silent house that night... <#0.45#> they found the mother — <#0.15#> Dee Dee Blanchard — <#0.15#> dead in her bedroom.
display: But when police entered that cold, silent house that night, they found the mother — Dee Dee Blanchard — dead in her bedroom.

text: And Gypsy Rose... <#0.45#> was gone.
display: And Gypsy Rose was gone.

text: Her wheelchair was still inside the house.
display: Her wheelchair was still inside the house.

text: The oxygen tanks and dozens of life-sustaining medicine bottles were still on the shelves.
display: The oxygen tanks and dozens of life-sustaining medicine bottles were still on the shelves.

text: All of America was stunned and asked one desperate question: <#0.3#> Who had caused the death of that devoted mother, and taken away a girl who, everyone believed, could not take a single step on her own and could die at any moment without her medication?
display: All of America was stunned and asked one desperate question: Who had caused the death of that devoted mother, and taken away a girl who, everyone believed, could not take a single step on her own and could die at any moment without her medication?

text: To get the clearest picture of the turning point in this case, we will now hear from the Investigator who handled this file directly.
display: To get the clearest picture of the turning point in this case, we will now hear from the Investigator who handled this file directly.

text: At first, we feared Gypsy Rose had been kidnapped and that her life was in danger.
display: At first, we feared Gypsy Rose had been kidnapped and that her life was in danger.

text: But just one day later, when officers found Gypsy Rose in Wisconsin, hundreds of miles from the scene... <#0.45#> a truth came to light that stunned doctors and investigators alike.
display: But just one day later, when officers found Gypsy Rose in Wisconsin, hundreds of miles from the scene... a truth came to light that stunned doctors and investigators alike.

text: When she walked into our interrogation room that day, Gypsy Rose was not in a wheelchair.
display: When she walked into our interrogation room that day, Gypsy Rose was not in a wheelchair.

text: She walked in... <#0.45#> on her own two feet.
display: She walked in on her own two feet.

text: No leukemia.
display: No leukemia.

text: No muscular dystrophy.
display: No muscular dystrophy.

text: No brain damage.
display: No brain damage.

text: And the person behind the plan that led to the death of that saintly mother... <#0.45#> was none other than her own little girl.
display: And the person behind the plan that led to the death of that “saintly” mother... was none other than her own little girl.

text: Welcome... <#0.45#> to the criminal psychology case files.
display: Welcome to the criminal psychology case files.

text: Today, we step inside the pink house in Missouri to decode one of the strangest and cruelest psychiatric syndromes ever hidden behind a mask of love: <#0.3#> Munchausen syndrome by proxy.
display: Today, we step inside the pink house in Missouri to decode one of the strangest and cruelest psychiatric syndromes ever hidden behind a mask of love: Munchausen syndrome by proxy.

text: To understand why a young woman would take such an extreme step against her own mother in order to survive, we first need to look at the real crime scene of this case.
display: To understand why a young woman would take such an extreme step against her own mother in order to survive, we first need to look at the real crime scene of this case.

text: That scene is not the bedroom in June 2015.
display: That scene is not the bedroom in June 2015.

text: The real crime scene... <#0.45#> is Gypsy Rose’s body, over the 23 years that came before.
display: The real crime scene is Gypsy Rose’s body, over the 23 years that came before.

text: Gypsy Rose was born in 1991, a completely healthy child.
display: Gypsy Rose was born in 1991, a completely healthy child.

text: But when she was just 3 months old, Dee Dee began taking her to the hospital, insisting that her daughter suffered from sleep apnea.
display: But when she was just 3 months old, Dee Dee began taking her to the hospital, insisting that her daughter suffered from sleep apnea.

text: From that point on, Dee Dee started building an enormous, fabricated medical history.
display: From that point on, Dee Dee started building an enormous, fabricated medical history.

text: When Gypsy was around 7, after a minor knee injury, Dee Dee declared that her daughter had a spinal cord injury and made the girl use a wheelchair for good.
display: When Gypsy was around 7, after a minor knee injury, Dee Dee declared that her daughter had a spinal cord injury and made the girl use a wheelchair for good.

text: She shaved Gypsy’s head, then told the child and the whole world that her hair had fallen out because of chemotherapy for leukemia.
display: She shaved Gypsy’s head, then told the child and the whole world that her hair had fallen out because of chemotherapy for leukemia.

text: But Dee Dee... <#0.45#> did not stop at lies.
display: But Dee Dee did not stop at lies.

text: Going back through thousands of pages of seized medical records, police found direct medical interventions on Gypsy’s body.
display: Going back through thousands of pages of seized medical records, police found direct medical interventions on Gypsy’s body.

text: Let us hear the Investigator present the details of this part of the file.
display: Let us hear the Investigator present the details of this part of the file.

text: To turn the script in her head into real symptoms in front of doctors, Dee Dee directly affected her daughter’s health in three ways documented in her medical records:
display: To turn the script in her head into real symptoms in front of doctors, Dee Dee directly affected her daughter’s health in three ways documented in her medical records:

text: First, she gave Gypsy high doses of anti-seizure medication... <#0.45#> even though she had no epilepsy — <#0.15#> drugs that, according to later reports, contributed to the loss of her teeth.
display: First, she gave Gypsy high doses of anti-seizure medication even though she had no epilepsy — drugs that, according to later reports, contributed to the loss of her teeth.

text: Second, she persuaded doctors to place a feeding tube into Gypsy’s stomach.
display: Second, she persuaded doctors to place a feeding tube into Gypsy’s stomach.

text: And third, by describing false symptoms to doctors, she convinced the hospital to perform an unnecessary salivary gland surgery on the girl.
display: And third, by describing false symptoms to doctors, she convinced the hospital to perform an unnecessary salivary gland surgery on the girl.

text: The big question for our investigation at the time was: <#0.3#> Why did an entire modern healthcare system, with hundreds of doctors, fail to notice?
display: The big question for our investigation at the time was: Why did an entire modern healthcare system, with hundreds of doctors, fail to notice?

text: As we pieced the file together, we found that Dee Dee had an extremely sophisticated modus operandi:
display: As we pieced the file together, we found that Dee Dee had an extremely sophisticated modus operandi:

text: She had worked as a nurse’s aide, so she knew medical terminology and how to describe textbook symptoms.
display: She had worked as a nurse’s aide, so she knew medical terminology and how to describe textbook symptoms.

text: In 2005, when Hurricane Katrina swept through Louisiana, Dee Dee used the disaster to claim that all of Gypsy’s original medical records and her birth certificate had been washed away by the flood.
display: In 2005, when Hurricane Katrina swept through Louisiana, Dee Dee used the disaster to claim that all of Gypsy’s original medical records and her birth certificate had been washed away by the flood.

text: From that moment on, Gypsy’s entire medical history was written down by new doctors from Dee Dee’s words alone.
display: From that moment on, Gypsy’s entire medical history was written down by new doctors from Dee Dee’s words alone.

text: Whenever a doctor began to suspect something — <#0.15#> like Doctor Bernardo Flasterstein, a neurologist who in 2007 noted a strong possibility of Munchausen by proxy — <#0.15#> Dee Dee simply stopped seeing that doctor and moved on to new doctors and new hospitals.
display: Whenever a doctor began to suspect something — like Doctor Bernardo Flasterstein, a neurologist who in 2007 noted a strong possibility of Munchausen by proxy — Dee Dee simply stopped seeing that doctor and moved on to new doctors and new hospitals.

text: In the pink house built by charity, the windows were always shut.
display: In the pink house built by charity, the windows were always shut.

text: Gypsy was not allowed to go to school because her mother said she had an intellectual disability.
display: Gypsy was not allowed to go to school because her mother said she had an intellectual disability.

text: Her age was falsely reported as 4 years younger than it really was, so that she would forever remain a minor under her mother’s absolute guardianship.
display: Her age was falsely reported as 4 years younger than it really was, so that she would forever remain a minor under her mother’s absolute guardianship.

text: A prison without bars... <#0.45#> built instead from prescriptions, IV tubes... <#0.45#> and the glow of charity.
display: A prison without bars, built instead from prescriptions, IV tubes and the glow of charity.

text: At this point, the biggest question anyone must ask is: <#0.3#> Why?
display: At this point, the biggest question anyone must ask is: Why?

text: What could a mother possibly gain by making her healthy child live like a sick person for more than two decades?
display: What could a mother possibly gain by making her healthy child live like a sick person for more than two decades?

text: Many people rushed to conclude that Dee Dee did it to profit from charity money, free trips to Disney World or a house from Habitat for Humanity.
display: Many people rushed to conclude that Dee Dee did it to profit from charity money, free trips to Disney World or a house from Habitat for Humanity.

text: But from the perspective of criminal psychology and forensic psychiatry... <#0.45#> money was only a side benefit.
display: But from the perspective of criminal psychology and forensic psychiatry, money was only a side benefit.

text: The core motive driving Dee Dee Blanchard’s behavior is widely believed to lie in a psychological disorder called Munchausen syndrome by proxy — <#0.15#> known in the modern psychiatric manual DSM-5-TR as factitious disorder imposed on another (FDIA).
display: The core motive driving Dee Dee Blanchard’s behavior is widely believed to lie in a psychological disorder called Munchausen syndrome by proxy — known in the modern psychiatric manual DSM-5-TR as factitious disorder imposed on another (FDIA).

text: To understand this disorder more deeply, I invited a criminal psychologist to share their analysis.
display: To understand this disorder more deeply, I invited a criminal psychologist to share their analysis.

text: Let us listen as the Psychologist walks us through the 3 psychological layers inside Dee Dee Blanchard’s mind.
display: Let us listen as the Psychologist walks us through the 3 psychological layers inside Dee Dee Blanchard’s mind.

text: When we examine the psychology of someone believed to have FDIA, like Dee Dee Blanchard, we have to go through 3 layers of motive, both unconscious and conscious.
display: When we examine the psychology of someone believed to have FDIA, like Dee Dee Blanchard, we have to go through 3 layers of motive, both unconscious and conscious.

text: The first layer... <#0.45#> is an addiction to the glory of the martyred saint.
display: The first layer is an addiction to the glory of the “martyred saint.”

text: In psychology, an ordinary fraudster fakes illness to collect insurance money and then disappears to enjoy it — <#0.15#> that is called malingering (faking illness for gain).
display: In psychology, an ordinary fraudster fakes illness to collect insurance money and then disappears to enjoy it — that is called malingering (faking illness for gain).

text: But a person with Munchausen syndrome is different: what they hunger for is not money, but attention, sympathy and admiration.
display: But a person with Munchausen syndrome is different: what they hunger for is not money, but attention, sympathy and admiration.

text: Before Gypsy, Dee Dee’s life was a chain of failures: estranged from her family amid accusations of petty theft, a marriage that fell apart when she was 24.
display: Before Gypsy, Dee Dee’s life was a chain of failures: estranged from her family amid accusations of petty theft, a marriage that fell apart when she was 24.

text: She was a faint shadow in society.
display: She was a faint shadow in society.

text: But the moment she took on the role of the brave single mother of a dying child... <#0.45#> Dee Dee suddenly became the center of the universe.
display: But the moment she took on the role of “the brave single mother of a dying child,” Dee Dee suddenly became the center of the universe.

text: Wherever she went, doctors respected her, neighbors were moved to tears, and local news stories portrayed her as a living saint.
display: Wherever she went, doctors respected her, neighbors were moved to tears, and local news stories portrayed her as a living saint.

text: Every time Gypsy was rushed to the emergency room, it was as if Dee Dee’s brain received a powerful shot of dopamine from the attention of the crowd.
display: Every time Gypsy was rushed to the emergency room, it was as if Dee Dee’s brain received a powerful shot of dopamine from the attention of the crowd.

text: But the addiction to attention was only the surface.
display: But the addiction to attention was only the surface.

text: Taking into account allegations from some of Dee Dee’s own relatives that she had harmed members of her family in the past, the Psychologist goes on to reveal the second and third layers — <#0.15#> where the cruelty reaches its peak.
display: Taking into account allegations from some of Dee Dee’s own relatives that she had harmed members of her family in the past, the Psychologist goes on to reveal the second and third layers — where the cruelty reaches its peak.

text: The second layer is a pathological fear of abandonment and a need for total control.
display: The second layer is a pathological fear of abandonment and a need for total control.

text: When Gypsy was born, Dee Dee saw in this child the one possession that would never be allowed to leave her.
display: When Gypsy was born, Dee Dee saw in this child the one possession that would never be allowed to leave her.

text: But a healthy child grows up, goes to school, makes friends, falls in love and leaves her mother.
display: But a healthy child grows up, goes to school, makes friends, falls in love and leaves her mother.

text: How do you keep a human being by your side... <#0.45#> forever?
display: How do you keep a human being by your side forever?

text: The dark answer that Dee Dee’s twisted mind found was: <#0.3#> Make the girl believe she is sick and completely dependent on her mother.
display: The dark answer that Dee Dee’s twisted mind found was: Make the girl believe she is sick and completely dependent on her mother.

text: When Gypsy believed she could not walk on her own and could not take care of herself, Dee Dee became the only one holding her daughter’s life in her hands.
display: When Gypsy believed she could not walk on her own and could not take care of herself, Dee Dee became the only one holding her daughter’s life in her hands.

text: And finally... <#0.45#> the third layer: the psychological signature of erasing an identity.
display: And finally, the third layer: the psychological signature of erasing an identity.

text: We paid special attention to the fact that Dee Dee regularly shaved Gypsy’s head and made her wear brightly colored children’s princess dresses even when she was over 20 years old.
display: We paid special attention to the fact that Dee Dee regularly shaved Gypsy’s head and made her wear brightly colored children’s princess dresses even when she was over 20 years old.

text: It was not only about faking cancer.
display: It was not only about faking cancer.

text: It was infantilization — <#0.15#> the stripping away of adulthood.
display: It was infantilization — the stripping away of adulthood.

text: She would not allow Gypsy’s body to grow into a woman’s.
display: She would not allow Gypsy’s body to grow into a woman’s.

text: In Dee Dee’s imagined script, Gypsy had to remain forever a fragile 7-year-old porcelain doll, held entirely in the palm of her hand.
display: In Dee Dee’s imagined script, Gypsy had to remain forever a fragile 7-year-old porcelain doll, held entirely in the palm of her hand.

text: When the case came to light, alongside the outrage at the mother, many people also began asking a skeptical question about Gypsy Rose herself.
display: When the case came to light, alongside the outrage at the mother, many people also began asking a skeptical question about Gypsy Rose herself.

text: Let us hear a very typical question from a viewer who followed the case.
display: Let us hear a very typical question from a viewer who followed the case.

text: There is one thing I just cannot understand: <#0.3#> She knew perfectly well that her legs were not paralyzed.
display: There is one thing I just cannot understand: She knew perfectly well that her legs were not paralyzed.

text: Every night, alone in her room, she would still get up and walk around normally.
display: Every night, alone in her room, she would still get up and walk around normally.

text: So why, in all those years, in front of hundreds of doctors, police officers and crowds, did Gypsy never once stand up from that wheelchair... <#0.45#> and expose her mother?
display: So why, in all those years, in front of hundreds of doctors, police officers and crowds, did Gypsy never once stand up from that wheelchair and expose her mother?

text: To answer this question, we cannot apply the thinking of a free adult to a child who grew up inside a glass cage.
display: To answer this question, we cannot apply the thinking of a free adult to a child who grew up inside a glass cage.

text: Let us return to the Psychologist to decode Gypsy’s silence through two powerful psychological mechanisms: learned helplessness and trauma bonding.
display: Let us return to the Psychologist to decode Gypsy’s silence through two powerful psychological mechanisms: learned helplessness and trauma bonding.

text: The concept of learned helplessness was first described by psychologist Martin Seligman and his colleagues in 1967.
display: The concept of learned helplessness was first described by psychologist Martin Seligman and his colleagues in 1967.

text: When an animal is exposed again and again to stress it cannot escape, and every attempt to resist is useless, the brain reaches a fixed conclusion: <#0.3#> All struggle is meaningless.
display: When an animal is exposed again and again to stress it cannot escape, and every attempt to resist is useless, the brain reaches a fixed conclusion: “All struggle is meaningless.”

text: From that moment on, even when the cage door is wide open... <#0.45#> the animal will lie still and endure, and never walk out again.
display: From that moment on, even when the cage door is wide open, the animal will lie still and endure, and never walk out again.

text: Now look at the world through Gypsy’s eyes, from the moment she was old enough to understand:
display: Now look at the world through Gypsy’s eyes, from the moment she was old enough to understand:

text: Every time they sat in front of a doctor, Dee Dee would hold Gypsy’s hand tightly.
display: Every time they sat in front of a doctor, Dee Dee would hold Gypsy’s hand tightly.

text: To outsiders, it was the tender gesture of a mother.
display: To outsiders, it was the tender gesture of a mother.

text: But to Gypsy... <#0.45#> it was a secret threat: <#0.3#> If she said even one wrong word, or showed that she was healthy, that grip would tighten like a silent warning.
display: But to Gypsy, it was a secret threat: If she said even one wrong word, or showed that she was healthy, that grip would tighten like a silent warning.

text: And when the door of the pink house closed after the appointment, harsh punishment and suffocating control would be waiting for her.
display: And when the door of the pink house closed after the appointment, harsh punishment and suffocating control would be waiting for her.

text: In fact, Gypsy did try to save herself.
display: In fact, Gypsy did try to save herself.

text: In the case file, the Investigator found an incident from 2011 — <#0.15#> an incident that completely extinguished this young woman’s last spark of hope.
display: In the case file, the Investigator found an incident from 2011 — an incident that completely extinguished this young woman’s last spark of hope.

text: Let us hear the details from the Investigator.
display: Let us hear the details from the Investigator.

text: According to accounts from Gypsy and others, in 2011, when she was about 19, she secretly left home to be with a man she had met at a science fiction convention, hoping he would help her escape.
display: According to accounts from Gypsy and others, in 2011, when she was about 19, she secretly left home to be with a man she had met at a science fiction convention, hoping he would help her escape.

text: But Dee Dee soon tracked her down... <#0.45#> at a hotel.
display: But Dee Dee soon tracked her down at a hotel.

text: There, in front of the man, Dee Dee produced paperwork with a false, younger birth date that made Gypsy appear to be a minor, and threatened to call the police.
display: There, in front of the man, Dee Dee produced paperwork with a false, younger birth date that made Gypsy appear to be a minor, and threatened to call the police.

text: Once again, people believed the saintly mother, and Gypsy was brought back to the pink house.
display: Once again, people believed the “saintly” mother, and Gypsy was brought back to the pink house.

text: Afterward, by Gypsy’s account, Dee Dee destroyed her phone and computer and warned her never to step out of the door again.
display: Afterward, by Gypsy’s account, Dee Dee destroyed her phone and computer and warned her never to step out of the door again.

text: That shock in 2011 sealed one belief in Gypsy’s mind: <#0.3#> The outside world would never believe a girl labeled as disabled; it would only believe her wonderful mother.
display: That shock in 2011 sealed one belief in Gypsy’s mind: The outside world would never believe a girl labeled as disabled; it would only believe her wonderful mother.

text: And beyond fear, the Psychologist points to another invisible thread binding the girl.
display: And beyond fear, the Psychologist points to another invisible thread binding the girl.

text: It is called... <#0.45#> trauma bonding.
display: It is called trauma bonding.

text: Dee Dee was the one causing Gypsy’s illnesses, yet Dee Dee was also the only person who held her every night, brushed her hair and called her Mommy’s little angel.
display: Dee Dee was the one causing Gypsy’s illnesses, yet Dee Dee was also the only person who held her every night, brushed her hair and called her “Mommy’s little angel.”

text: The mix of harsh control and smothering indulgence paralyzed Gypsy’s ability to recognize boundaries.
display: The mix of harsh control and smothering indulgence paralyzed Gypsy’s ability to recognize boundaries.

text: When every legal way out seemed sealed off, a mind that had been held down for 23 years turned to the most extreme exit.
display: When every legal way out seemed sealed off, a mind that had been held down for 23 years turned to the most extreme exit.

text: Online, Gypsy met Nicholas Godejohn — <#0.15#> a young man from Wisconsin whose lawyers later argued at trial that he was on the autism spectrum.
display: Online, Gypsy met Nicholas Godejohn — a young man from Wisconsin whose lawyers later argued at trial that he was on the autism spectrum.

text: Some observers have compared what developed between these two isolated young people to folie à deux — <#0.15#> a madness shared by two.
display: Some observers have compared what developed between these two isolated young people to folie à deux — a madness shared by two.

text: Gypsy has said she came to believe that only if her mother were gone could she live a life of her own.
display: Gypsy has said she came to believe that only if her mother were gone could she live a life of her own.

text: And on a night in June 2015... <#0.45#> the tragedy erupted, when Gypsy opened the door for Godejohn to walk into the pink house...
display: And on a night in June 2015, the tragedy erupted when Gypsy opened the door for Godejohn to walk into the pink house...

text: In a Missouri courtroom, the case of Gypsy Rose Blanchard sparked an intense legal and ethical debate.
display: In a Missouri courtroom, the case of Gypsy Rose Blanchard sparked an intense legal and ethical debate.

text: Legally, helping to plan an act that led to the death of one’s own mother is undeniably a serious felony.
display: Legally, helping to plan an act that led to the death of one’s own mother is undeniably a serious felony.

text: But Greene County prosecuting attorney Dan Patterson said that, although he believed he could have won a first-degree murder conviction, it would not have been fair, given the years of abuse Gypsy had suffered at her mother’s hands.
display: But Greene County prosecuting attorney Dan Patterson said that, although he believed he could have won a first-degree murder conviction, it would not have been fair, given the years of abuse Gypsy had suffered at her mother’s hands.

text: In 2016, under a plea agreement, Gypsy Rose pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 10 years in prison — <#0.15#> the minimum for that charge in Missouri.
display: In 2016, under a plea agreement, Gypsy Rose pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 10 years in prison — the minimum for that charge in Missouri.

text: Perhaps the most heartbreaking words came from Gypsy herself, in a TV interview after her release: <#0.3#> I also had more freedom in prison than I ever had with my mother.
display: Perhaps the most heartbreaking words came from Gypsy herself, in a TV interview after her release: “I also had more freedom in prison than I ever had with my mother.”

text: At the end of December 2023, after serving 85% of her sentence, she was released on parole.
display: At the end of December 2023, after serving 85% of her sentence, she was released on parole.

text: Looking back at the entire case file, so that similar tragedies can no longer hide in the dark, we will hear the Psychologist and the Investigator sum up 4 red flags that help the community recognize Munchausen syndrome by proxy early.
display: Looking back at the entire case file, so that similar tragedies can no longer hide in the dark, we will hear the Psychologist and the Investigator sum up 4 red flags that help the community recognize Munchausen syndrome by proxy early.

text: The first sign: <#0.3#> A child or dependent person has a dense, unusual, never-ending medical history, while objective test results always contradict the caregiver’s description.
display: The first sign: A child or dependent person has a dense, unusual, never-ending medical history, while objective test results always contradict the caregiver’s description.

text: The second sign: <#0.3#> Symptoms appear only when the caregiver is present, and clearly improve as soon as the patient is separated or under camera surveillance.
display: The second sign: Symptoms appear only when the caregiver is present, and clearly improve as soon as the patient is separated or under camera surveillance.

text: The third sign: <#0.3#> The caregiver seems overly eager about invasive medical procedures, likes to show off the child’s illness on social media for praise, and immediately changes doctors whenever someone asks a skeptical question.
display: The third sign: The caregiver seems overly eager about invasive medical procedures, likes to show off the child’s illness on social media for praise, and immediately changes doctors whenever someone asks a skeptical question.

text: And the fourth sign: <#0.3#> The victim is isolated from school, friends and other relatives on the pretext of protecting their health.
display: And the fourth sign: The victim is isolated from school, friends and other relatives on the pretext of “protecting their health.”

text: The file on the pink house in Missouri is now closed, but its echo remains a sharp reminder of the many-sided nature of the human mind.
display: The file on the pink house in Missouri is now closed, but its echo remains a sharp reminder of the many-sided nature of the human mind.

text: True love always aims to help a child grow up healthy, independent and able to walk on their own two feet.
display: True love always aims to help a child grow up healthy, independent and able to walk on their own two feet.

text: When love is twisted into a cage, when care becomes a tool to satisfy an adult’s selfish ego... <#0.45#> then what wears the robe of an angel can sometimes be as devastating as any crime.
display: When love is twisted into a cage, when care becomes a tool to satisfy an adult’s selfish ego... then what wears the robe of an angel can sometimes be as devastating as any crime.

text: Thank you to our guests for analyzing this case file with us, and thank you for listening to the very end of today’s story.
display: Thank you to our guests for analyzing this case file with us, and thank you for listening to the very end of today’s story.

display: Leave your perspective in the comments, keep a clear head, and see you in the next episode.
